problem_type: Program-initiated canvas viewport moves after content is created, imported or landed
symptom: User 2026-09-25: "老是动画布，我刚才用付费卡点击之后画布就闪动一下，然后我就找不到那个镜头生成去哪里了……有时候导入的时候不在中心展示导致找不到，好像修过，但类似问题反复发生". Real-machine reproduction on origin/main d8824a0c5 (Windows, used fixture): clicking the toolbar's new-image button panned the whole canvas so the previously visible card left the screen.
direct_cause: Creation paths each asked the canvas to move after the fact: useCreatedNodeVisibilityPan revealed every single new node (and zoomed out for consecutive creates), applyCanvasToolCall dispatched a focus (zoom ≥ 100% and centre) for one node or requested a fit for batches and switched category, multiShotCanvasLanding requested another fit 360 ms later (the two moves overlap into the reported flash), the asset library placed uploads at a fixed (120, 90) and then requested a fit, image grid split requested a fit, and duplicate/rerun/sidebar-regenerate dispatched focus. Default placements were fixed canvas coordinates unrelated to the viewport, which is why a reveal was needed at all.
class_root: No owner decided where new content lands relative to what the user sees, so every creation path compensated by moving the viewport afterwards; any new creation path added another viewport mover.
affected_population: Every canvas user creating, importing, duplicating or landing content (toolbar, paste, Agent, paid card, storyboard, asset library, grid split)
Users whose Agent writes into a category other than the one they are looking at

invariant_owner_layer.why: canvasVisibleArea owns where new content lands relative to the visible area; canvasArrivalModel owns which arrivals still need pointing out; the structure test pins the only callers allowed to move the viewport (explicit user actions).

entry_points: Toolbar / empty-state / prompt & skill library / selection-to-node creation without explicit position (addNode default)
Agent create_canvas_nodes (single and batch) and storyboard landing
Asset-library upload and image grid split
Variant duplicate, rerun duplicate, sidebar regenerate-derived, ⌘D duplicate
Explicit user moves: fit, reset, zoom, minimap, sidebar locate, locate-source badge, toast locate, notification deep link, open-stage, edge hint

external_sources.purpose: schedule() divides by the extent width every frame (k = w / l[2]); with a 0-width cached extent every animated frame is NaN, which is why animated viewport moves stay on the in-house per-frame direct writer
XYPanZoom caches the pane extent from a ResizeObserver and feeds it to d3-zoom; installed @xyflow/system 0.0.81 still does this (dist/esm/index.js XYPanZoom cachedExtent)

invariants: The canvas viewport moves only on explicit user actions; requestCanvasFit and the focus event are called only from an allowlisted set of user-triggered entries
Content created without an explicit position lands at the visible-area insertion point of its category
New content that is not visible is announced by one edge hint; the viewport moves only when the user clicks it
Programmatic animation frames do not write the workbench store; the settled viewport is recorded once

door_reduction.why_not: Before: 5 requestCanvasFit callers, 10 focus-event dispatchers (4 automatic), 6 animateViewportTo writers (3 in the reveal pan) — 21 viewport movers, most automatic. After: every remaining mover is a user click (fit/reset in the shell, explicit locate in the focus effect, the edge hint, open-stage, the allowlisted locate dispatchers), plus the placement owner and its three consumers that replace moving the viewport with landing in view. Each surviving door is either the single owner or a distinct user action; the allowlist test fails on any new mover.

generality_proof: New creation paths no longer need to move anything: placement defaults to the visible area in the store's addNode (the choke point every single-node creation passes through), batches are shifted as a block by the same owner, and anything still off-screen or in another category is detected by diffing the store's node set against a baseline tied to the loaded-canvas identity — so the hint covers every present and future creation path without a per-entry call. The two remaining global movers are pinned to an allowlist by a structure test.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Where new content lands relative to what the user currently sees (single points and whole batches)
Which arrived nodes have not been seen yet and where the edge hint points
The only animated viewport writer, used by explicit user moves; records the settled viewport once

same_class_entry_points.evidence: requestCanvasFit removed; nodes go through applyCanvasToolCall (block placed in view) and the edge hint covers the rest; multiShotCanvasLanding.test.ts asserts no fit and no category switch
focus dispatch and fit/category switch removed; batch layout shifted into view via placeBlockInVisibleArea; applyCanvasToolCall.test.ts asserts canvasFitNonce stays 0 and active category unchanged
requestCanvasFit removed; allowlist test would fail if it came back
focus dispatch removed; canvasControlsStructure.test.ts asserts the file no longer mentions the focus event
fits only at category open when content already existed (shouldFitOnOpen, user answer to question 4); nodes arriving later never trigger it
Explicit user click on the production status card; the only allowlisted requestCanvasFit caller

recurrence.reason: Reveal/fit behaviour was added and patched repeatedly (2026-09-05 canvas-walkthrough-stage-width, 2026-09-09 canvas-acceptance-red, 2026-09-20 materialization-viewport, 2026-08-29 variant focus recovery); each new creation path added its own mover, and the user reports the class keeps coming back.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs FOCUS_GENERATION_NODE_EVENT plus rg "'nomi-focus-generation-node'" (a literal dispatch in CategoryTree.tsx was found and unified)
rg "position: \{ x: 1[0-9]{2}, y:" src/workbench for fixed default placements (addNode default, asset library, empty state)

prevention.invariant: New content lands in the visible area; the viewport moves only on explicit user actions
prevention.failure_mode: If the visible area is unknown (canvas never mounted) placement falls back to the caller's own layout and the edge hint announces anything off-screen once the canvas is visible; nothing moves the viewport automatically
prevention.strategy: Own placement at the store choke point, detect arrivals by diffing the store instead of instrumenting entries, delete every automatic mover and pin the remaining explicit ones to an allowlist

legacy_paths.rationale: Deleted the created-node reveal pan (single reveal, consecutive-create zoom-out, ⌘D reveal, undo restore) and the target tracker that only served it; removed the fit/focus requests from agent creation, paid-card landing, asset upload, grid split, duplicate/rerun/sidebar regenerate; removed the undo-triggered viewport restore in the focus effect; useAutoFitOnLoad no longer fires on nodes appearing later

dependency_lifecycle.current: @xyflow/system 0.0.81 with d3-zoom 3.0.0: animated setViewport/setCenter/fitView produce NaN frames when the cached pane extent is 0, and interrupted transitions never resolve
dependency_lifecycle.target: React Flow's own animated viewport helpers (setViewport({ duration }))
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Explicit user moves keep a short animation for orientation; the framework's animation path is unsafe while the pane can measure 0x0, so the in-house per-frame direct writer (viewportAnimationCoordinator) is retained
exit_criteria: An @xyflow/system or d3-zoom release guards zero-width extents in the transition (no NaN transform when the pane is 0x0) and resolves interrupted transitions
A walk that hides and re-shows the canvas mid-animation shows no blank canvas using setViewport({ duration })

migration: No persisted state changes. Remembered viewports keep working; only the automatic moves are gone.
residual_risks: Crash-recovery event-tail replay after project open adds nodes without changing the loaded-canvas identity, so those nodes can show an edge hint once
Agent batches that do not fit the visible area stay below existing content; the user relies on the edge hint
Per-node spiral avoidance can still push a single new node just outside a crowded view; the edge hint covers it
